conversationalSummary.text: TODAY at Baleal looks like no reliable window, mainly because the wind fit is poor for Meio da Baia and Surfline is coming through rough. There might be a little size around lunch with the low rising tide, but it’s the kind of conditional sandbar setup that can feel soft fast when the swell/push isn’t clearly there. I’d check Surfline and MEO Beachcam before leaving, but unless the cams show a lot cleaner/wider peaks than expected, it’s probably not worth chasing—save the drive.

best.explanation: Meio da Baia looks like a fun-sized window for Worth checking, Low confidence: 0.6-1.1 m, 111 kJ, 9 s period, consistent 72/100, and wind is the main risk.  An inconsistent Baía spot that can work well when north-northwest swell reaches the bay; this is best for bodyboard sessions when the bay is clean, there is enough period and size, and the forecast shows a defined wave; 6-9s at low tide can still make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia punchy.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot.
best.shortExplanation: Meio da Baia is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

ranked.explanation: Cantinho da Baia looks like a fun-sized window for Safe fun, Medium confidence: 0.6-0.9 m, 145 kJ, 9 s period, consistent 71/100, and wind is the main risk.  A forgiving sandy bay with lots of take-off points; this is best for easy wave count and cleaner faces when the north wind is bothering exposed beaches; 6-9s at low tide is basically flat or too weak in the sheltered bay; worth keeping on the radar because Surfline is showing it above Poor while most other local spots are Poor..  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; 6-9s at low tide is basically flat or too weak in the sheltered bay; SwellMap rating 3/10 Poor — caution.
